source.revision: Code accompanying this IR; baseline 0a949cf12f226a63b0db6244f9fc2a1e3fef78d1 plus accepted journey changes, reviewed 2026-11-16
source.description: Source-derived current behavior, including the accepted Retry, Settings review and pointer-open changes. Fixed fictional fixtures; no live provider requests. Affected browser flows and native offline checks passed. Scaffold: repo-kit 4914a36.

included: Browser configuration draft Save, conflict/uncertain delivery blocking, explicit reload confirmation and dirty navigation.
Managed shared connections, explicit account authorization and key-removal confirmation; shared definitions are separate from secrets.
Custom Call Create / Check file stages a candidate; only Save and select loads local code. Restore/default selection stays explicit.
Saved Speak preview generates in memory and only plays after a user action.
Reviewed layout hints group navigation contexts and route/recovery neighborhoods; coordinates are presentation only, not time or rank.

Review latest retains non-conflicting local edits, requires Mine/Latest for conflicting fields and removed items, masks credentials, and applies to the draft without saving. Cancel/read failure keeps the original context.
omitted: Standalone credential setup, every provider catalog option, invalid-record reset, notification rules and optional native helper installation are not expanded.
The app has more Settings sections than these graph regions; the inventory in README records the remaining source owners.
No real account, key, local script, billing request, browser setting or audio playback is used.
A finite scenario projection, not the full Cartesian product of app state. System buttons simulate possible source-code outcomes.
No proposed optimization: Comparison is intentionally absent.
The expanded Settings conflict/reload route uses the Preset editor; identical owner checks for Action editing are not duplicated into UI states.

Terminal landmarks end this scoped review; they do not imply that the real application quits. Compound navigation labels name their menu/section steps; route counts are model transitions, not measured click counts.

The atlas illustrates one conflicting name. The implementation also handles additions, removals, already-delivered writes and paired credential/endpoint edits; these are covered by model and browser checks rather than separate landmarks.
